Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll start with the workspace contract in `README.md`, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and guidance. I’ll use the fish-control bookshelf exactly at the protocol’s required decision point and record any transfer explicitly in the policy notes.

I’ve confirmed this is a single editable policy candidate with two mandatory provenance/guidance updates and no local CFD run. I’m now applying two relevant workspace skills: the required fish-control bookshelf for architecture transfer, and the visual-evidence skill so both moving-window views inform the diagnosis before I touch the controller.

The visual comparison is now anchored: both sampled candidates self-propel through a shallow capture arc in zero inflow, with an alternating top-down wake and tail-connected 3D structures; the lateral-response residual variant repeats capture slightly earlier and at lower integrated distance cost. I’m cross-checking that narrow improvement against actuation/load traces and the inherited parent logs before choosing a genuinely new mechanism.

The bookshelf consultation is now timely under the structured protocol: the inherited parent has converged on repeated promotion of the same lateral-residual capture, while recent alternatives (line-of-sight-rate feedforward and geometric-bearing residualization) changed code without improving semantics. I’ll use the shelf only to select a mechanism-level invariant, not to tune carrier gains.

The shelf points to one compatible next mechanism that respects the inherited failures: a response-gated redirect, triggered by normalized closure loss, while preserving the full traveling-wave carrier. This avoids the disproven wave-energy relief, static bends, target-line-rate feedforward, geometric phase subtraction, and yaw-moment rejection. Because that source family informs the edit, I’m reading its source notes and will include the required transfer/falsification block.

I’ve selected one narrow, falsifiable candidate: preserve the demonstrated controller and add a separate approach-only, phase-compatible redirect that activates when target-aligned closure drops relative to swimming speed. It will not add mean curvature or reduce both half-cycles; it only attenuates the half-cycle opposing the measured velocity-course correction. I’m recording the visual diagnosis and transfer provenance before editing the policy, as required.

The candidate policy is now edited. I’m also distilling a missing inherited negative result into reusable guidance: the prior yaw-moment residual was cleanly phase-demodulated and slightly reduced peak load, yet still worsened target progress. That sharpens the rule from “residualize responses” to “residualization alone does not make a signal control-worthy.”

The candidate and durable lesson are both materially updated. Since Julia is not available in this workspace, I’ll use the required deterministic check-runner now; it validates the policy contract and guidance delta without launching CFD.

The dedicated check-runner could not start because its fixed model is unsupported by this account. I’ll still satisfy the workspace check contract by reading the immutable runner specification and executing its checks locally; if needed, I’ll use a normal validation agent as a second independent pass.

Two specified checks pass: the guidance update is material and evidence-backed, and the boundary checker confirms only the permitted solver file changed. The Julia executable is absent, so I’ve run the deterministic parameter-schema comparison directly (no missing fields) and am asking a normal validation agent to independently apply the immutable check-runner specification without CFD.

Independent validation has confirmed the material guidance delta, boundary restriction, parameter schema, fixture-state coverage, and return shape. The only unavailable check remains execution under Julia itself; the validator is finishing a static syntax and finite-output audit so I can report that limitation precisely.

All feasible final checks pass on the finished snapshot: guidance provenance, editable-boundary enforcement, schema completeness, fixture-state coverage, balanced Julia structure, finite mirrored output, and nonempty required files. Formal CFD was not run. The exact Julia interpreter smoke remains unavailable solely because this workspace has no Julia executable.

Completed exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): adds a closure-qualified, phase-compatible posterior redirect while preserving the validated carrier.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): contains visual diagnosis, evidence comparison, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:176): materially records the negative yaw-moment-residual result and reusable boundary.

Checks passed for guidance provenance, editable boundaries, parameter schema, state coverage, syntax structure, and finite mirrored output. Julia execution was unavailable because `julia` is not installed. No CFD was run.
